data.claim: No. The lease was bound to the very tree the commit was made in, so check_commit's same_tree rule would have counted it; the lease had EXPIRED. Its last clock-moving renewal was 14:13:52 (the update --globs renewals at 14:15/14:22/14:28 carry no 'at' and do not move renewed_at); commit 4dd7b3e at 15:00:03 is 46 min later, past ttl_s 1800 + grace_s 120; the agent heartbeated at 15:00:06, 3 s after the commit. The hook's message was true but misleading: 'You hold: (no live lease)' plus 'claim the work' instead of 'your lease in this tree lapsed, heartbeat it'.
data.falsifier: If the lease folded at 15:00:03 were live, or bound to a different tree than the committing one, identity would be the cause.
data.mechanism: services/enforce.check_commit only iterates active_leases; an expired lease bound to this tree is invisible, so the message cannot say it lapsed. DDFLOW_AGENT is already honoured (api.setup.hooks -> _load resolves it into cfg.agent.id).

data.summary: The commit hook says 'You hold: (no live lease)' and prescribes 'ddflow claim' when the committer's own lease, bound to the very tree being committed in, has merely LAPSED (no heartbeat past ttl_s+grace) and nobody has taken it over. check_commit only looks at active_leases, so it cannot say the lease lapsed or name the remedy (heartbeat it as its holder). Seen on B-local-config-surfaces at 4dd7b3e (lease last renewed 14:13:52, commit 15:00:03) and misdiagnosed as an identity bug (B5fde61b8a9, research R2440394451). Expected: name the lapsed lease, when, and 'ddflow --agent <holder> heartbeat <id>'; still warn/refuse per policy.

data.body: Fixes bug B3e050cb66a (and B5fde61b8a9, refuted as an identity bug by R2440394451: the real cause was a lapsed lease). check_commit iterates only active_leases; add: expired, not-taken-over leases that would have been 'mine' (holder == me or bound to the committing tree) and whose globs cover an uncovered staged path are named in the message with when they lapsed and the remedy 'ddflow --agent <holder> heartbeat <id>'. The outcome is unchanged (warn or block per policy): a lapsed lease is not a pass. Tests: lapsed own-tree lease is named with the heartbeat remedy; a genuinely unclaimed path still warns with the claim remedy and no lapsed-lease text; a lapsed lease in ANOTHER tree held by another agent is not offered; DDFLOW_AGENT owner committing from another tree is covered, a different agent is warned.
data.title: The commit hook names a lapsed lease bound to this tree (or held by this agent) and says to heartbeat it, instead of '(no live lease)' and 'claim' (fixes bug B3e050cb66a)

The real defect: check_commit only reads active_leases, so it printed '(no live lease)' + 'claim' instead of 'your lease lapsed, heartbeat it'. Also probed: DDFLOW_AGENT is already honoured by the hook (api.setup.hooks -> _load resolves it); test_the_hook_reads_ddflow_agent_from_the_environment passes on main.

titles: `ddflow.services.enforce.check_commit` — the "mine" predicate (`holder == me or bound to the committing tree`)

data.body: Fixes B3e050cb66a (and B5fde61b8a9, refuted as an identity bug by R2440394451: the real cause was a lapsed lease): check_commit also scans expired, not-taken-over leases that would have been mine (holder == me or bound to the committing tree) covering an uncovered path, and no other live lease overlaps; names when it lapsed, 'ddflow --agent <holder> heartbeat <id>', and for a tree-only match the takeover path (recover, release, claim). Fixes B9aeb141b9a: its root cause (claim via as_agent recording the parent's tree) was B5c32cbb5c1 = B7c7a0d9222, fixed in 89fa18e1; DDFLOW_AGENT is honoured by the hook (tested end to end); what remained is the message blaming the holder: when nothing declared an identity and the path is held by another lease, the hook says it derived the name from the tree and, per holder, where its item's tree is and DDFLOW_AGENT=<holder>. Fixes Bf1fc9823fe: test_a_claimed_commit_succeeds_with_no_agent_configured_anywhere scrubs DDFLOW_AGENT for its claim too. Outcomes unchanged (warn/block per policy).

Found and fixed one: the derived-identity hint keyed on 'cfg.agent.id empty', but the hooks command (api._load) writes the derived name INTO cfg.agent.id, so the hint never reached the real hook. Fixed in b02b05d (keys on cfg.sources['agent.id'] == 'derived'); end-to-end test test_the_derived_identity_hint_reaches_the_real_hook fails on f23b78f, passes after. Probed: lapsed lease overlapping another live lease anywhere is not offered (per-lease guard, 2 tests); a bare claim of an expired lease is refused and release+plain claim takes over (test); holder heartbeat revives an expired own lease (test); declared non-holder gets no derived hint (test); a lease marked expired_at with a recent clock is pre-existing active_leases behaviour, untouched. No further finding.

The 'mine' predicate (holder == me or bound to this tree) was duplicated by the new lapsed scan; factored into one _counts_as_mine used by both. Takeover advice reuses the exact path api/lifecycle._claim_blocker and docs/RECOVERY.md give (recover, release, claim) rather than a new one. api/lifecycle._in_leased_tree is the same tree test on a different input (stored path vs lease) in another layer; left as is, not widened into this item's globs.
